title: Teams meeting policy: which meeting features does each user get?
summary: The page names the wrong PowerShell operation for assigning a policy to a batch of users: Microsoft documents New-CsBatchPolicyAssignmentOperation, not Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. The listed control paths and calls are supported, and the cited pages that previously returned throttling errors opened successfully in this check.

claims.claim: Meeting policy settings can be edited at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Edit.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies or Events policies.
2. Choose the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -<parameter> <value> is a template for updating the settings of an existing meeting policy.
claims.quote: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies that can be assigned to particular users to control Teams features related to meetings.

claims.claim: Group assignment is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Group policy assignment > Add.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
To groups: Go to the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Group <group ID> -PolicyName <policy name> -Rank <rank> assigns a meeting policy to a group with a ranking.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Group d8ebfa45-0f28-4d2d-9bcc-b158a49e2d17 -PolicyName "Retail Managers Meeting Policy" -Rank 1

claims.claim: Individual assignment is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Manage users > Assign users.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
To specific users: Select your policy, select Manage users > Assign users, enter the names of specific users in the search bar, select Add, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <user> -PolicyName <policy name> assigns a meeting policy to an individual user.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity reda@contoso.com -PolicyName "Student Meeting Policy"

claims.claim: The Meeting recording toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Turn the Meeting recording toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true allows meeting recording under that policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.claim: The Transcription toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows meeting transcription under that policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Live captions is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Live captions.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. From the drop-down for Live captions, select Not enabled, but users can enable(default value) or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled turns off live captions for users with that policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off live captions for users with this policy, run the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: The Copilot default setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Enabled sets the Only during the meeting default for meetings and events organized by users with this policy.
claims.quote:
To allow users to use Copilot Only during the meeting in meetings and events created by organizers with this policy:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Enabled

claims.claim: A Teams meeting policy is a set of settings controlling the meeting features available to organizers and participants.
claims.quote: you can use meeting and events policies to control the features that are available to organizers and participants of meetings and events in your organization.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be managed in the Teams admin center or with the Teams PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Policies are managed through the Teams Admin Center or the Teams PowerShell module

claims.claim: Every user has one effective meeting policy.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each policy type.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The Global policy applies when the user has neither a direct custom assignment nor an inherited group policy.
claims.quote: If a user isn't directly assigned a policy or isn't a member of any groups that are assigned a policy, the user gets the global (Org-wide default) policy for that policy type.

claims.claim: Administrators can edit the Global meeting policy.
claims.quote: You can edit the global policy and any custom policies that you create.

claims.claim: Administrators can create named custom meeting policies.
claims.quote:
Select Add.
3. Enter a name and description for the policy.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one events policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Events policies are separate from meeting policies and have their own recording settings.
claims.quote: Meetings and events each have their own recording policies that you can manage.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Events policies have their own transcription settings.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Events policies.
Turn the Transcription for events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: Microsoft documents three implementation types for meeting and events policies.
claims.quote:
Policies are implemented in one of the following ways:
Per-organizer
Per-user
Per-organizer and per-user

claims.where: What it is: implementation table; Why it matters
claims.claim: For a per-organizer policy, participants inherit the organizer's policy.
claims.quote: When you implement a per-organizer policy, all participants inherit the policy of the organizer.

claims.claim: Who can bypass the lobby is Microsoft's example of a per-organizer policy.
claims.quote: For example, Who can bypass the lobby is a per-organizer policy

claims.claim: A per-user policy allows or prevents the feature for each user.
claims.quote: When you implement a per-user policy, the policy allows or prevents a given feature for each user.

claims.claim: Meet now in channel meetings is Microsoft's example of a per-user policy.
claims.quote: For example, Meet now in channel meetings is a per-user policy.

claims.claim: Combined policies restrict participants based on both their policy and the organizer's policy.
claims.quote: certain features are restricted for participants based on their policy and the organizer's policy.

claims.where: controls[3].note; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Recording is per-organizer and per-user: both the organizer and recording initiator need permission.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.where: controls[1].note; controls[2].note; What it is; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: A directly assigned policy takes precedence over inherited group policies and the Global policy.
claims.quote: If a user is directly assigned a policy (either individually or through a batch assignment), that policy takes precedence.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Without a direct assignment, the user inherits the highest-ranked applicable group policy.
claims.quote: the user inherits the policy of the group assignment that has the highest ranking.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Ranking 1 is the highest group assignment ranking.
claims.quote: Smaller the number, the higher the ranking with 1 being the highest ranking.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Policies can be assigned to batches of users in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
To assign a policy to users in bulk:
In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Users.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets, final sentence
claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy is the PowerShell operation for assigning a policy to a batch of users.
claims.quote: You use the New-CsBatchPolicyAssignmentOperation cmdlet to submit a batch of users and the policy that you want to assign.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Policies can be assigned to individual users, to batches of users or to a group in the admin centre. In PowerShell, Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy assigns a policy to an individual user or a group; New-CsBatchPolicyAssignmentOperation submits a batch assignment.' The cited assignment article documents the distinction.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Transcription is per-organizer and per-user: the organizer and person starting recording or transcription must have it enabled.
claims.quote: For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: Transcription is On by default for new meeting policies.
claims.quote: This setting is On by default for new policies.

claims.claim: Live captions is a per-user policy.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy and applies during a meeting.

claims.claim: DisabledUserOverride allows users to turn on live captions.
claims.quote: Live captions are off by default, but users with this assigned policy can turn on live captions during meetings or events.

claims.claim: Copilot in Teams meetings requires an add-on Microsoft Copilot license for intended users.
claims.quote: An add-on Microsoft Copilot license for intended users.

claims.claim: Other Copilot parameter values are EnabledWithTranscript, EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn and Disabled.
claims.quote:
On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript
On with transcript saved by default | EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn
Off | Disabled

claims.claim: Live translated transcription requires the meeting organizer to have Teams Premium.
claims.quote: The meeting or event organizer must have a Teams Premium license for attendees to use live translated transcription.

claims.claim: Live translated captions require the meeting organizer to have Teams Premium.
claims.quote: The meeting or event organizer must have a Teams Premium license for attendees to use live translated captions.

claims.claim: Organizers with Teams Premium can use meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: Organizers with a Teams Premium license can use their meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.

claims.claim: Meeting recordings are stored in the organizer's OneDrive or SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.claim: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits
claims.claim: AllowCloudRecording does not configure or validate recording storage.
claims.quote: -AllowCloudRecording controls whether users can record meetings; it doesn't configure or validate recording storage.

claims.claim: The meeting policy overview and policy-assignment pages state no license or meter for meeting policies themselves as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting policies license meter price policy assignment group propagation time large groups. Read meeting-policies-overview, policy-assignment-overview and assign-policies-users-and-groups on Learn; none states a license or meter for meeting policies themselves.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A direct assignment silently beats a group assignment
claims.claim: Direct assignments must be removed to inherit group policies, and Microsoft documents removing them in bulk.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can unassign policies in bulk to remove direct assignments so Global (Org-wide default) or group assignments take effect.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Group policy assignments propagate only to direct members.
claims.quote: Group policy assignments are only propagated to users who are direct members of the group.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; What to check
claims.claim: Group assignments do not propagate to members of nested groups.
claims.quote: The assignments aren't propagated to members of nested groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; What to check
claims.claim: Groups with HiddenGroupMembership enabled cannot use group policy assignment.
claims.quote: Groups with the HiddenGroupMembership setting enabled can't use group policy assignment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps
claims.claim: Class Teams have HiddenGroupMembership enabled by default.
claims.quote: Class Teams have this setting enabled by default.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps
claims.claim: Propagation of group policy assignment to members runs in the background.
claims.quote: the propagation of the policy assignment to members of the group is performed as a background operation and might take some time, depending on the size of the group.

claims.where: Risks and limits; Open questions: group propagation
claims.claim: The group-assignment article gives no group-size-specific propagation time.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting policies license meter price policy assignment group propagation time large groups. Read all of assign-policies-users-and-groups; it says propagation might take some time depending on group size, but supplies no size-specific duration.

claims.where: Risks and limits; Open questions: group propagation
claims.claim: Microsoft's general policy guidance says changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policies cannot be tidied freely
claims.claim: A policy cannot be deleted while users remain assigned to it.
claims.quote: You can't delete a policy if users are assigned to it. You must first assign a different policy to all affected users, and then you can delete the original policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policies cannot be tidied freely
claims.claim: A policy name cannot be changed after creation.
claims.quote: After you create a policy, its name can't be changed.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: An organizer turning Copilot Off for a meeting or event also turns off recording.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Copilot for their meeting or event, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: An organizer turning Copilot Off for a meeting or event also turns off transcription.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Copilot for their meeting or event, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: The Copilot Off policy value sets a default organizers can override per meeting or event.
claims.quote: When organizers with this policy create meetings and events, Copilot's default value in their meeting options is Off. Organizers can change this value to Only during the meeting or During and after the meeting.

claims.claim: External participants cannot record meetings except under third-party compliance recording.
claims.quote: External participants can't record meetings except when it's a Teams third-party compliance recording.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: Recordings that cannot upload to OneDrive or SharePoint are stored temporarily and deleted unless downloaded within 21 days.
claims.quote: If a recording can't be uploaded to OneDrive or SharePoint, it's temporarily stored in async media storage and must be downloaded within 21 days. Otherwise, the recording is deleted.

claims.claim: Changing a group assignment ranking in the Teams admin center requires removing and re-adding the assignment.
claims.quote: To change the ranking of a group assignment, you need to remove the group policy assignment first. Then, follow the steps above to assign the policy to a group.

claims.claim: PowerShell Grant cmdlets can change the ranking of an existing group assignment.

After you assign a policy to a group, you can use the appropriate Grant cmdlet to change that group's policy assignment as follows:

claims.claim: The recording page documents channel recording download control only as a PowerShell parameter, not an admin-center toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams ChannelRecordingDownload admin center toggle PowerShell only. Read meeting-recording in full and Learn excerpts from manage-meeting-recording-options; the recording article documents -ChannelRecordingDownload with PowerShell and no UI toggle.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not name audit events recording a change to a meeting policy or where those events appear.

claims.where: What to check: List custom meeting policies; Governance controls

List custom meeting policies with Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and confirm each one is still assigned to a group or user.
The corresponding table row instead gives Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -<parameter> <value>.
claims.fix: Replace the checklist bullet with 'Review custom meeting policy settings and confirm each policy is still assigned to a group or user.' This removes the unrepresented read operation without adding a controls row.
